refused.candidate: Nazaha (Oversight and Anti-Corruption Authority) monthly case statement: a bank employee arrested for taking gifts and paid travel in return for depositing cash of unknown source into a commercial entity's accounts; the arrest was made 'in cooperation with the Presidency of State Security and the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA)'.
refused.source_title: Nazaha reveals details of 16 corruption cases; Among them officers and government employees / Nazaha continues to clamp down on corruption, initiates criminal cases
refused.test_failed: Inversion test. SAMA is the body that helped DETECT and arrest, not the subject. The accused is an unnamed 'bank employee' and the bank is not named; neither article says he worked for SAMA. Filing it would credit Saudi Arabia with a corruption case for catching wrongdoing.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: A Nazaha statement (or Saudi court/Public Prosecution notice) that names the accused's employer as the Saudi Central Bank / مؤسسة النقد / البنك المركزي السعودي, rather than listing SAMA as a cooperating agency.

refused.candidate: Carlos Federico Paredes, president of the Banco Central de Reserva from June to November 2019, was sentenced to eight years by the Tribunal Primero de Sentencia de Santa Tecla on 25 November 2020 for estafa (fraud) against three women over promised land lots in Santa Elena, Antiguo Cuscatlan; a Camara de lo Penal upheld it on 18 August 2021; the Sala de lo Penal of the Corte Suprema de Justicia then annulled the conviction and ordered sobreseimiento definitivo because the offence was time-barred, holding the limitation period ran from the 2008 facts.
refused.source_title: Sala anula condena contra expresidente del Banco Central
refused.test_failed: Two separate failures. (1) Conduct in a different capacity: the fraud was a 2008 private land sale, eleven years before he held office at the BCR; the bank, its money and its officials-in-office are not the subject. (2) Even if it counted, the outcome maps to 'conviction annulled (time-barred)', which is a not-counted status.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: A readable source showing conduct by Paredes (or any other BCR official) committed while in office at the Banco Central de Reserva, or involving BCR funds or BCR decisions - for example a Corte de Cuentas de la Republica reparo or juicio de cuentas naming the BCR as the audited entity.

refused.candidate: On 13 June 2018 Egypt's Administrative Control Authority (هيئة الرقابة الإدارية) arrested the 'director of the supervision and oversight sector at one of the banks' (مدير قطاع الرقابة والإشراف بأحد البنوك) for taking bribes from the owner of a private exchange company in return for overlooking its violations, including trading foreign currency outside legal channels, and for leaking the dates of planned inspections of that company. He was referred to the public prosecution.
refused.source_title: فيديو| الرقابة الإدارية تضبط مسئولا بنكيا سرب مواعيد تفتيش شركات (Parlmany) and فساد في شركات الصرافة.. ضبط مسؤول بنكي لتسريبه مواعيد تفتيش النقد الأجنبي (Sout Al Omma)
refused.test_failed: No-fabrication rule. The conduct would qualify squarely - a banking supervisor taking bribes from a supervised exchange company and leaking its inspection dates is a supervisory failure with named conduct, a date and an arresting body. But both articles say only 'one of the banks' and name no institution. Supervising exchange companies and foreign-currency inspections is a Central Bank of Egypt function and 'قطاع الرقابة والإشراف' is the CBE's own sector name, so the inference is strong - but inference is not a source stating the fact, so it is not filed.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: Any readable source - an ACA statement on aca.gov.eg, a prosecution or court notice, or a news report - that names the arrested man's employer as the Central Bank of Egypt (البنك المركزي المصري). This is the closest candidate of the round and should be the next round's first target.

refused.candidate: SAACB (ديوان الرقابة المالية والإدارية) Annual Report 2020, qualified opinion on the Ministry of Finance's consolidated final accounts: 'لم يتم الإفصاح عن المبلغ المستحق على وزارة المالية لصالح سلطة النقد الفلسطينية' - the amount the Ministry of Finance owed the Palestine Monetary Authority was not disclosed; the unrecorded year-end balance was about 2,130,918 dinars, tied to exchange-company licence fees the Authority had collected for the Treasury and that were later redirected to the Authority as its own revenue.
refused.source_title: ديوان الرقابة المالية والإدارية - التقرير السنوي 2020
refused.test_failed: Counterparty-only / already-settled. The audited body is the Ministry of Finance; the PMA is the creditor whose balance the Ministry failed to disclose. The brief already records that Palestine holds a Ministry of Finance finding that is not counted, and this is the same kind of thing.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: A SAACB report (or Palestinian Anti-Corruption Commission / Anti-Corruption Court decision) in which سلطة النقد الفلسطينية itself appears as the audited or investigated entity, with a finding against the Authority or its staff.

refused.candidate: SAACB Annual Report 2020, Ministry of Labour emergency worker support programme: employees of the Palestine Monetary Authority appear among beneficiaries who received emergency aid without meeting the programme's criteria ('مستفيدين يعملون في سلطة النقد الفلسطينية').
refused.source_title: ديوان الرقابة المالية والإدارية - التقرير السنوي 2020
refused.test_failed: Subject test. The criticised body is the Ministry of Labour and its disbursements; the PMA is named only as the employer of some people who were paid. No conduct is attributed to the Authority or to any official of it.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: A finding that PMA staff obtained the aid by misrepresenting their employment or income, or that the PMA certified eligibility - i.e. conduct attributed to the Authority or its people rather than to the Ministry.

refused.candidate: Two Samoa Audit Office / Ministry of Finance Internal Audit and Investigations Division matters reported to Parliament: (a) a former Ministry of Health Procurement Specialist who produced falsified Tenders Board letters of approval with forged signatures to support $212,000 in payments for goods and services never supplied, investigated by the I.A.I.D. on 17 June 2014 and resigning on 30 June 2014, reported to the Speaker on 16 December 2016; (b) Faumuina Tiatia Liuga, former Cabinet Minister responsible for the Samoa Land Corporation, implicated by the Chief Auditor's report, with a parliamentary committee recommending charges in December 2014.
refused.source_title: Tenders Board approval forged, Parliament told / Former public servant implicated in forgery not with Ministry of Finance / Faumuina faces more allegations
refused.test_failed: Subject test. Neither matter involves the Central Bank of Samoa. The subjects are the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Finance's accounts division and the Samoa Land Corporation. The brief already notes Samoa's existing Ministry of Finance finding is not counted.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse: A Controller and Chief Auditor report, Officers of Parliament Committee report, or Samoan court record in which the Central Bank of Samoa or a CBS official is the audited or accused party.

refused.source_title: Report on the Implementation of Recommendations from selected Government related entities (Office of the Auditor General, Bermuda, June 2023)
refused.test_failed: Lead closed, not a candidate. Appendix III was read. The Bermuda Monetary Authority does not appear. The entities listed as audits in progress are: Berkeley Institute Capitation Grant Account (2015, 2016-2022), Bermuda Educators Council (2016-2019), Sandys Secondary Middle School Capitation Grant Account (2016, 2017-2018), Trustees of the National Sports Centre (2017, 2018-2021), Bermuda Economic Development Corporation (2019) and Bermuda Gaming Commission (2020, 2021). searched_no_result.status: confirmed blank against a named document
searched_no_result.detail: Auditor-General's Office of Singapore, Annual Report FY2023/24 (https://www.ago.gov.sg/files/ARs/ar_fy2023_24.pdf). Read Part II 'Financial Statements Audits', paragraph 1(c) and its footnote 1, plus the full list of audit observations in Parts I-III. The Monetary Authority of Singapore appears exactly twice and in neither case as a body with lapses: it is listed among statutory boards given an UNMODIFIED audit opinion for 2023/24, and footnote 1 states 'The Monetary Authority of Singapore is audited by AGO annually' because the MAS Act names no other auditor. This is the strongest possible negative for Singapore: the supreme audit institution audits the central bank every year and recorded no observation against it. Agencies with lapses in that report were MOE, MHA, IMDA, Sport Singapore, Nanyang Polytechnic, BCA, NParks, Sentosa Development Corporation, MSF and ECDA.

searched_no_result.detail: Genuinely closed for this vein. Qatar's State Audit Bureau (ديوان المحاسبة) does not publish entity-level findings; the only 2026 coverage is of Law amendments EXPANDING the Bureau's powers (criminal penalties and financial disclosure - Peninsula/Qatar Tribune art. 243490, QNA 2026-7/8, Mondaq 1823470), not of any audit result. Shura Council finance committee coverage (QNA Russian-service items, July 2026) names no institution. Remaining results were Commercial Bank of Qatar (CBQ) corporate governance reports - a listed commercial bank, not the central bank - and a Qatar Tribune piece on QCB 'enhancing resilience' of the financial sector, which is the bank acting, not being found against.

searched_no_result.query: Bahrain National Audit Office annual report "Central Bank of Bahrain" violations findings diwan
searched_no_result.detail: Read the Daily Tribune's report on Bahrain's National Audit Office 2024 annual report ('Secret loans, soaring deficit spark alarm in audit report', https://www.newsofbahrain.com/bahrain/112220.html). The Central Bank of Bahrain is NOT named as an audited body and is not criticised. Audited bodies named are ministries, state-owned bodies, Gulf Air, Bapco Energies, the Sunni Waqf Directorate, public hospitals and the National Health Regulatory Authority. The report's debt findings - public debt up 7% to BD17.9bn for 2023, plus BD3.9bn of ministry and government-body loans never entered on the official debt register - do not identify which institution keeps the register, so they cannot be attributed to the CBB. Other search hits were the CBB's own Compliance and Enforcement Annual Report 2024, which is the CBB acting against licensees (inversion trap), and further Daily Tribune NAO round-ups (40124, 40293, 57776, 8191, 27231).

searched_no_result.detail: No audit or inquiry document reachable. Brunei's Auditor General report is not published online in a form the search returned; every result was either a BDCB/AMBD self-published document on cms.bdcb.gov.bn (annual reports, regulatory notices), a commercial bank's own report (Baiduri), or the FATF/APG Mutual Evaluation Report of Brunei Darussalam 2023. The MER is a methodology assessment of the AML/CFT system, not a finding of misconduct at the central bank. Legislative Council (Majlis Mesyuarat Negara) proceedings naming AMBD/BDCB were not reachable through this search.

searched_no_result.detail: No finding against the Central Bank of Samoa. leads_not_opened.lead: Egyptian Administrative Control Authority year-in-review round-ups that may name the Central Bank of Egypt as the employer of the supervision-sector director arrested on 13 June 2018 for taking bribes from an exchange company and leaking its inspection dates. This is the highest-value unopened lead of the round.

MAS is audited by Singapore's Auditor-General every single year under the MAS Act, so each AGO annual report is an independently checkable document. Only FY2023/24 was read. The other twelve returned reports remain unread.

Unread portions of the SAACB Annual Report 2020: characters 100,000-200,000 and 300,000-500,000 of the PDF. Also AMAN's SAACB reports index page, and the unread final 6,000 characters of the AMAN PMA risk study.

Brunei's FATF/APG Mutual Evaluation Report 2023 - not a misconduct finding, but its immediate-outcome write-ups on supervision may describe a specific supervisory failure by BDCB with a date and an episode, which would qualify. Also BDCB's own annual reports for disciplinary/anti-corruption notes, the vein that closed one country already.

The Tribunal de Contas de Cabo Verde's own site and its Relatorio e Parecer sobre a Conta Geral do Estado were never reached - no search result pointed at them. Also an oversight directory page for Cabo Verde's auditor, and Cape Verde gazette bulletins that may carry Tribunal de Contas decisions.

Bahrain NAO annual reports for years other than 2024, via Daily Tribune round-ups, and the Council of Representatives' public accounts follow-up. The BD3.9bn of unregistered government loans in the 2024 report is worth tracing: if a later document says the Central Bank of Bahrain keeps or failed to keep the debt register, that becomes a supervisory-failure record rather than an unattributable figure.

Samoa Audit Office / Officers of Parliament Committee reports listed on palemene.ws, and the March 2019 charging of senior Samoan officials over misuse of public assets. Also the CBS annual reports' own staff-discipline sections.

Corte de Cuentas de la Republica's own publications were never reached directly - no search result returned cortedecuentas.gob.sv. Its monthly completed-audit lists are reported by El Mundo, which would identify whether the BCR has ever been an audited entity.
